summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted following a syncopal episode with no seizure activity, occurring after standing and preceded by dizziness and slurred speech. She had significantly reduced oral intake for three weeks following hiatal hernia surgery, leading to hypovolemia and orthostatic hypotension. Imaging, including CT head/neck and MRI, showed no acute neurological pathology. Chronic abdominal pain and nausea persisted, and an EGD revealed a narrowed anastomotic junction, which was dilated. Due to ongoing malnutrition and inability to tolerate oral intake, a post-pyloric Dobhoff feeding tube was placed, and enteral nutrition was initiated. Her symptoms improved with IV fluids, optimized medications, and tube feeds. She was discharged home with service to continue tube feeding, follow up with GI, PCP, bariatric surgery, neurology, and complete outpatient autonomic and ENT evaluations.
